newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on export talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on export talk.

text.p: CBOT old crop soybean futures ended with double-digit gains for the second day amid ideas prices had fallen enough in recent weeks to attract export demand, traders said.

"That sell-off last week caught the Brazilian FOB basis going in the other direction and put us into favorable price comparisons with Brazil," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer. "That uncovered some new business."
U.S. exporters could not confirm the deals but there was widespread talk that two cargoes of old crop soybeans were sold out of the Great Lakes to Europe.
Also, Asian traders said Chinese companies have been buying significant quantities of U.S. soybeans since early July when prices collapsed.
July continued to soar, lifted by ideas there would be no deliveries. None have been posted yet and traders noted several key commercial firms exited short positions this week.
But CFTC on Tuesday said deliverable soybean stocks in Chicago rose to 1,850,000 bushels as of July 3, up from 1,405,000 the previous week.
Soybeans ended 26 to 11-1/4 cents per bushel higher with August up 26 at $7.48.

New crop months also ended higher but advances were limited by continued good growing weather in the U.S. Midwest and prospects for a record crop this fall. Some analyst have predicted production at 2.8 billion bushels.

Commercials were the primary buyers of the August but pit sources said volume in the old crop months was thin. Cargill Inc bought two million bushels August, Continental Grain bought one million August and Tenco Inc bought two million August and 500,000 July, traders said.
Funds were light buyers of the November. Merrill Lynch and Refco Inc each bought one million November while Smith Barney bought 1.5 million November, floor sources said.

Bull spreads were active with ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp spreading two million August/November at $1.34 to $1.40, premium August. Traders said LFG spread one million July/August at $0.47 to $0.43, premium July. Goldenberg-Hehmeyer spread 0.5 million July/November at $1.81 to $1.83, premium July.

In options trade, Smith Barney bought 2,000 September $6.50 calls at 19 to 26 cents, Louis Dreyfus sold 600 September $8.50 calls at 2-1/2 cents and Lind-Waldock sold 500 August $7.25 calls at 21 cents.
Volatilities again surged. August closed at 39-3/4 percent, up from 35-3/4 on Tuesday and 30-1/2 percent on Monday. Volatility in the November was pegged at 20 percent, unchanged from Tuesday.

Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 80,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 64,561 contracts. Options volume was pegged at 30,000 contracts, against Tuesday's 33,262 contracts.
